question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}-2{X}_{2} & ∼N({\mu }_{1}-2{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+4{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(9-8,8+8) \\  & ∼N(1,16).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =1$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{16}=4.$ 

We want to find $P(Y\le 4).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\le 4) & =P(Z\le \frac{4-1}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.75) \\  & =Φ(0.75)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.75)≈0.7734.
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(Y\le 4)≈0.77.
$$
